name: lsu_accept
mechanisms: storage.global.acceptance_sm (new: per-SM acceptance queue of global-memory requests LDG / STG / LDGSTS / atomics; the read barrier and the memory-hierarchy access start at its service start)
memory.l1.service.sector_bytes_per_cycle (installed 127.71 / 126.97 measured, no engine read point today)
question: Round 38 attribution (TR3-TUT-PERSIST-NAIVE-C04, 0.53; `$A/diag/pcstalls2/bw`, local replay `~/tmp/acc37/persist`): hardware spends 12.5 k of 40.6 k cycles on instructions that overwrite the address register of an LDGSTS issued 8 instructions earlier (long_scoreboard, 14-90 cycles per execution) -- the LDGSTS's read barrier is released only when the LSU accepts the request; in the engine the request's L2-port acceptance equals its issue cycle (8 sectors occupy 2 cycles of a 124 B/cycle port with 256 outstanding slots). How long after issue does the LSU accept a global-memory request, how does that acceptance scale with the number of requests already queued by this warp and by other warps on the SM, with the request's bytes, and is the queue shared with the shared-memory path (LDS / LDSM)?

engine_rules_declared_before_data.baseline: present engine: acceptance = first L2 / DRAM port_acquire start (round 38), practically the issue cycle; LDS / STS / LDSM take the per-SM kind-6 queue storage.shared.acceptance_sm (affine in 128 B wavefronts, slope ~1.0 cycle).
engine_rules_declared_before_data.Q (per-SM LSU acceptance queue): every global-memory request (LDG / STG / LDGSTS / ATOMG / REDG; TMA excluded -- it has its own service_start) enters a per-SM in-order queue at issue; service time = a_fixed + b * wavefronts, wavefronts = ceil(request bytes / 128); the read barrier is released at the queue's service start, and the memory-hierarchy access (L1 / L2 / DRAM path) starts at the service start instead of the issue cycle. Leaf storage.global.acceptance_sm: cycles affine(shared_wavefronts) with slope b and intercept a_fixed, enabled per device.
engine_rules_declared_before_data.Q-shared: as Q, but the queue is the SAME per-SM queue as storage.shared.acceptance_sm (LDS / STS / LDSM wavefronts delay global requests and vice versa).
engine_rules_declared_before_data.decision between Q and Q-shared: the mix cell (below) decides: if the LDGSTS acceptance slope in the mix cell equals the LDGSTS-only slope plus the LDS acceptance cost of the interleaved LDS instructions (installed storage.shared.acceptance_sm per wavefront) within 15 %, Q-shared; if it equals the LDGSTS-only slope within 15 % (the LDS traffic does not delay LDGSTS acceptance), Q; otherwise neither is installed and the table is reported.

probe: tools/microbench/lsu_accept/probe/lsu_accept.cu: one CTA of 32*W threads, W in {1, 2, 4, 8} (warp w on SMSP w % 4), bar.sync before every repetition, each warp's lane 0 records clock64 t_s before and t_w after the window; medians over warps x launches x reps (first rep dropped). Window = D back-to-back global requests on D DISTINCT 64-bit pointer registers p_1..p_D (per-lane coalesced: lane * bytes, 32 lanes -> 32 * bytes per request; each request its own 128 B-aligned region, regions distinct per warp and per k so no sector is shared), followed by ONE `add.s64 p_D, p_D, <imm>` on the LAST request's pointer register (the WAR on the read barrier of request D) and then t_w; after t_w: cp.async.wait_all / a dependent use of the loaded registers and bar.sync so the next repetition starts drained. D in {1, 2, 4, 8, 16}. Variants: `ldgsts16` (cp.async.cg.shared.global 16 B per lane, distinct smem destinations), `ldgsts8`, `ldgsts4` (8 / 4 B per lane: cp.async.ca), `ldg16` (ld.global.v4.b32 into 4 distinct destination registers per request), `ldg4` (ld.global.b32), `stg16` (st.global.v4.b32 from registers initialised before t_s), `mix` (ldgsts16 with one LDS.128 (ld.shared.v4.b32 from a per-warp region written before the window) inserted after every LDGSTS: window = D LDGSTS + D LDS + WAR), `lds` control (D ld.shared.v4.b32 on D distinct address registers + WAR on the last: the installed kind-6 queue, must reproduce storage.shared.acceptance_sm). All windows are straight-line inline asm volatile; the pointers are made per-lane and opaque the way contention_v3 does (added to a per-lane zero loaded from a global buffer). --launches 16 --reps 65, two runs per device.
sass_gate: tools/microbench/lsu_accept/sass_check.py: the window between the two SR_CLOCKLO reads contains exactly D instructions of the variant's class (LDGSTS.* / LDG.* / STG.* / LDS.* ; mix: D LDGSTS + D LDS) in order, then exactly one IADD3 / IMAD.IADD-type instruction writing the last request's low pointer register (identified by register number), and nothing else; the WAR instruction's control-word wait mask must include the read barrier (rbar) set by the last request (recorded and checked); the D requests must carry distinct address registers. Control words of all window instructions are recorded.

derivation.fit: per (variant, W): OLS of T over D -> slope s (cycles per request) and intercept c; residual <= 5 %, runs <= 5 % or 1 cycle -> usable
derivation.per-wavefront cost: b(variant) = s(variant, W=1) / wavefronts(variant) with wavefronts = 32 * bytes / 128 (ldgsts16 / ldg16 / stg16: 4, ldgsts8: 2, ldgsts4 / ldg4: 1); the bytes variants must agree on b within 15 % for an affine-in-wavefronts leaf, else the leaf is knots over wavefronts (1, 2, 4) and recorded as experimental
derivation.fixed part: a_fixed = c(W = 1) - (the WAR instruction's own issue cost: control-word stall of the last request + 1) - the clock-read overhead measured by a D = 0 cell (window = WAR only on an unrelated register) -- the D = 0 cell is part of every variant
derivation.sharing across warps: s(variant, W) / s(variant, 1) must be ~W (per-SM queue) for Q / Q-shared to be installed with scope sm; if it stays ~1 up to W = 4 and ~2 at W = 8 the queue is per SMSP (report; install scope smsp instead); anything else -> report only
derivation.mix: s(mix) compared with s(ldgsts16) + b_lds * 4 where b_lds is the installed storage.shared.acceptance_sm slope (LDS.128: 4 wavefronts) -- see the decision above; the lds control's s must reproduce 4 * installed slope within 15 % or the run is unusable for the mix decision
derivation.ldg vs ldgsts: if s(ldg16) and s(ldgsts16) agree within 15 % one leaf serves LDG / LDGSTS / STG; otherwise the leaf is partitioned by access kind (load / async_copy / store) with each variant's own slope

decision: install Q or Q-shared (per the mix rule) when: ldgsts16 / ldg16 / lds W = 1 cells usable, W-scaling ~W within 20 % at W = 2 and 4, and b agrees across byte variants within 15 % (affine) or knots are used (experimental). Evidence measured when all used cells have residual <= 5 % and runs <= 5 %; experimental otherwise. Nothing is installed when the W = 1 slope of ldgsts16 is <= 1.5 cycles per request on a device (the present port model already yields that) -- then the round-38 attribution is wrong for that device and the table is reported.
install: common mechanism storage.global.acceptance_sm (event issue, timing_row kind: a NEW timing kind `global_acceptance_sm`, operation_classes LDG / STG / LDGSTS / ATOMG / REDG / LD / ST (LD / ST only when the MACC resolves to a non-shared space), partition by access kind if needed); <arch>/leaves with cycles affine(shared_wavefronts: slope b, intercept a_fixed) or knots; converter: the class binding goes through program_tables like kind 5 / 6 (py == cpp gate); engine: the new kind serialises on a per-SM queue (its own `global_accept_next_[sm]`, or `shared_accept_next_[sm]` for Q-shared), accept_start = max(accept_start, queue start), and the memory-hierarchy call uses the queue start as `now` for the request (the request's sectors are issued to L1 / L2 / DRAM at acceptance); CTest fixtures: 8 LDG with the row -> WAR at 1 + 8 * s; two warps on one SM -> 16 * s; A/B 500 x 2 against $A/merge/rbg38.
not_allowed: no case-cycle tuning; no values from other machines; no threshold or variant change after data; TMA / bulk requests keep their own service_start leaves and are not touched.

addenda.written_before: any version-2 run; after reading h100-r7 (b300-r3 still queued on the B300 pool)
addenda.text: (reading of h100-r7; decision none, nothing installed) Probe: seven builds were needed before ptxas left the window alone (it sank LDS / STG past t_w, folded the D pointers into one base register + immediates, and the first opaque forms shared a base); the final probe loads a per-(k, lane) offset table so every request owns a distinct 64-bit register. Gate 28 / 48 kernels: the `lds` control is unrealised (plain ld.shared without a consumer in the window is sunk below t_w on sm_90a whatever the pinning), stg16 D >= 2, mix D >= 4, ldgsts4 / ldg4 D = 8 and ldgsts16 D = 16 fail on folded address registers or a WAR wait mask that does not name the last request's read barrier -- those D points are excluded, the fits use the remaining points. Measured per-request slopes (cycles per request, W = 1 / 2 / 4 / 8): ldgsts16 4.00 / 4.67 / 10.51 / 19.95 (intercept 13.0 at W = 1); ldgsts8 4.00 / 4.03 / 5.03 / 26.6; ldgsts4 4.00 / 4.03 / 5.03 / 26.6; ldg16 5.10 / 5.23 / 10.64 / 20.21; ldg4 4.11 / 4.04 / 10.81 / 25.97; stg16 6.22 / 11.43 / 24.19 / 89.90; mix 11.33 / 16.02 / 29.97 / 64.35. Reading: (1) a global request's read barrier is released ~4 cycles per queued request after issue at W = 1, independent of the request's bytes (4 / 8 / 16 B per lane all 4.00) -- a per-request cost, not a per-wavefront one, so the affine-in-wavefronts leaf of this protocol does not fit; (2) the cost scales sub-linearly with warps on distinct SMSPs (1.00 / 1.17 / 2.63 / 4.99 for W = 1 / 2 / 4 / 8), which is neither the per-SM queue (W) nor a per-SMSP queue (1 up to W = 4) this protocol declared -- it is consistent with a two-stage structure, a per-SMSP stage of ~4 cycles per request in front of a per-SM stage of ~2.5 cycles per request (W = 2: max(4, 5) = 5 vs 4.67; W = 4: 10 vs 10.5; W = 8: 20 vs 20.0), which version 2 must declare before measuring again; (3) with W = 4 warps each issuing 8 LDGSTS, this predicts the last request's acceptance ~80 cycles after issue -- the 14-90 cycles per execution the round-38 attribution saw on TR3-TUT-PERSIST-NAIVE-C04; (4) ldg16 is 5.1 vs ldgsts16 4.0 (partition by access kind in v2); stg16 scales super-linearly (6 / 11 / 24 / 90: the store path saturates something else -- the store-L2 port model may already cover part of it); the mix cell cannot decide Q vs Q-shared without the lds control. Version 2: a chain-with-consumer LDS control (each LDS result feeds the next address so ptxas cannot sink it, as the shared protocol's k_issue cells do), per-request leaf (intercept + slope in requests, not wavefronts), the two-stage candidate, and both devices.
